notes: Every frame is 256x192 pixels and stored rotated 90 degrees; I rotated each one upright and upscaled, and cropped/zoomed into detail regions. Even so the images are soft, so anything smaller than roughly a hand is at the edge of what can be named honestly. Confidence values reflect that.

The capture is an open-plan space. Frames 01-04 look across the living room into a dining area (white pedestal table, white chairs, tulips) and on into a kitchen (grey units) through a wide opening rather than a door. I included those items because they read as the same continuous space, but if the intended room boundary is the living area alone, the dining table, dining chairs, kitchen counter and vase of flowers should be dropped.

Frame 17 looks through an open doorway into a separate bedroom: a bed with a grey duvet on a dark base, a black nightstand, a framed portrait on a dark blue wall, and grey carpet. I deliberately did NOT list those as objects in this room, since they are clearly in an adjoining room.

Frames 05 and 06 (three garden windows, roman blinds, radiators, floor palm) cannot be geometrically tied back to the living-room frames from these stills alone. The flooring matches and they fall between the brick-wall frames and the fireplace frame in capture time, so I treated them as the same room, but this is an assumption.

Sofa counting is the least certain call here. I see a brown suede sofa with a grey pom-pom throw (frames 01-04), a brown suede sofa with navy and cream cushions (frames 10-12), and a third seat draped in a plain white sheet (frames 01, 04). They are never all in one frame, so I cannot fully exclude that two of these are the same sofa recorded at different times with the throw moved.

Two different glass-fronted display cabinets appear: an all-white four-panel one beside the staircase (frames 09, 12, 13) and a lower one with orange/pine-framed glass doors on the opposite side (frames 01, 03). They hold figurines, dolls and wine glasses, which I did not itemise individually.

A dark object with pale horizontal banding appears at the bottom-left of frame 08 and again to the right of the display cabinet in frame 09. It may be a carved wooden chest, a fire screen, or a magazine rack; I could not resolve it and left it off the list.
A black bag or box sits on the floor at the right edge of frame 03. Nameable as 'something black on the floor' but not confidently identifiable, so it is omitted.
A small glass dome or cloche with a red object inside sits on the fireplace hearth in frame 07; I folded the red item into the candle entry but the dome itself is too indistinct to name separately.

The two sheets lying on the floor (frames 00 and 17) are printed pictures on plain paper rather than hung artwork. They look like markers placed for the scan, but I have reported them literally as what is visible.

The framed-picture count of 9 is a best estimate: roughly 5-6 small frames plus a round decorative wall plate in the dining-area gallery wall, 2 white-framed watercolours on the dark panel, 1 above the chest of drawers, and 1 tall gilt piece on the brick wall. The gallery-wall frames are too small and blurred to count exactly.
White ceramic ornaments sit on the sill at the far-left edge of frame 05, but they are cut off and out of focus, so I did not name them.
Ceiling downlight and wall socket counts are lower bounds from what is framed; both fixture types almost certainly continue outside the visible field.
